claims.text: Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 is a near-equiatomic, chemically disordered high-entropy alloy.
Near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys such as Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 are used in thermal-insulation applications.
Strong chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys produces atomic-mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Local chemical disorder produces significant bond-strength fluctuations.
Disorder-induced mass and force-constant fluctuations reduce phonon lifetimes.
Force-constant and related elemental fluctuations enhance phonon scattering or acoustic-phonon attenuation in high-entropy materials.
Enhanced scattering associated with local chemical, mass, and strain fluctuations lowers lattice thermal conductivity.

A machine-learning model using local-environment, force-constant-fluctuation, and simulated-phonon-lifetime descriptors will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than current empirical or simplified ab initio models.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error by at least 20% relative to existing empirical or simplified ab initio methods.
High-dimensional disorder descriptors allow machine learning to capture nonlinear contributions from mass, bond, and force-constant fluctuations.
Traditional predictive models average out disorder effects and fail to account for their full spectrum.
Explicitly representing disorder-induced fluctuations and their relationship to phonon-scattering rates will improve lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
The proposed model will accurately predict phonon lifetimes and scattering rates in addition to lattice thermal conductivity.
Predicted broadened acoustic-phonon spectral features will closely match inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering measurements.
The approach is applicable from room temperature to approximately 700 K, where phonon scattering dominates thermal transport.
The predictive improvement is primarily limited to near-equiatomic solid-solution HEAs and may fail for compositionally asymmetric, phase-separated, long-range-ordered, or multiphase alloys.

contradictions.description: The principal outcome is a 20% relative error reduction versus baseline models, but the falsification rule instead uses an absolute prediction error above 20% and does not require evaluating the baseline models. Thus, the stated rule can pass even without the claimed relative improvement, or fail despite achieving it.
